response.reason: The mantissa-reduction threshold 1.65 leaves z up to ~0.2453, so the truncated atanh series (through z^7) has a systematic error of about 7.5e-7 near m=1.65 — already ~75% of the 1e-6 absolute tolerance — before any FP32 rounding. For large inputs (e.g. x near 54000, exponent 15, result ~10.9) single-ulp rounding of `high` and of the final sum is ~4.8e-7 each, so worst-case total error plausibly reaches ~1.5e-6, exceeding the fixed 1e-6 tolerance; a standard sqrt(2)-style reduction (z<=0.172) would be needed for safe headroom.
